title: Qubits, Bloch Sphere, Pauli Algebra, and One-Qubit Gates

items.title: Qubit spaces and states
items.statement_or_definition:
The **qubit space** is the one-qubit register $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ of [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)=(e_0,e_1)$. This basis is orthonormal by [[thm-qc-computational-basis-orthonormal]]. A **qubit state** is a density operator on $Q_2$ in the sense of [[def-qc-density-operator]], namely a non-negative endomorphism of trace one. A **pure qubit state** is a pure-state ray on $Q_2$ in the sense of [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]. The Bloch coordinates and their state-space constraints are defined and proved in the following items on this page.

The term qubit here names the two-dimensional register and its mathematical state space. No physical preparation or measurement postulate is part of this definition.
proof_obligations: Fix basis order and derive real coefficients from Hermitian trace-one coordinates.

items.title: The Pauli matrices
items.statement_or_definition:
In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.
proof_obligations: Verify adjoints, products and traces directly using the root-linear-first matrix convention.

items.title: Pauli matrix algebra and trace identities
items.statement_or_definition:
For the matrices $X,Y,Z$ of [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], each is self-adjoint and unitary, and $X^2=Y^2=Z^2=I$. Distinct Pauli matrices anticommute. For $j,k\in\{x,y,z\}$,
$$\sigma_j\sigma_k=\delta_{jk}I+i\sum_{\ell\in\{x,y,z\}}\epsilon_{jk\ell}\sigma_\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j\sigma_k)=2\delta_{jk}.$$
Here $\sigma_x=X,\sigma_y=Y,\sigma_z=Z$, $\delta_{jk}=1$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\epsilon$ is the alternating symbol with $\epsilon_{xyz}=1$. Also $\operatorname{tr}(I)=2$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j)=0$.
proof_obligations: Compute all nine products and track the sign determined by the displayed Y matrix.

items.title: Bloch coordinate maps
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $Q_2$ be the qubit space of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $Q_2$ in the sense of [[def-qc-density-operator]]. Define its candidate Bloch coordinates in $\mathbb C^3$ by
$$r_j(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\sigma_j)\quad(j\in\{x,y,z\}),\qquad \mathbf r(\rho):=(r_x(\rho),r_y(\rho),r_z(\rho)).$$
For any $\mathbf r=(r_x,r_y,r_z)\in\mathbb R^3$, define the associated Hermitian-matrix candidate
$$\rho(\mathbf r):=\frac12\bigl(I+r_xX+r_yY+r_zZ\bigr).$$
Write $\mathbf r\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}:=r_xX+r_yY+r_zZ$ and
$$\|\mathbf r\|_2:=\sqrt{r_x^2+r_y^2+r_z^2}.$$
The next theorem proves that these trace coordinates are real and that every Hermitian trace-one $2\times2$ matrix is uniquely $\rho(\mathbf r)$; the positivity theorem determines which real-coordinate candidates are states.
proof_obligations: Show coordinates are real and recover rho from the orthogonal Pauli basis.

items.title: Exact one-qubit gates and rotations
items.statement_or_definition:
In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.
proof_obligations: State angle, axis and basis conventions and verify each matrix is unitary; controlled gates retain displayed scalars.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of Bloch coordinates
items.statement_or_definition:
For every $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^3$, the matrix $\rho(\mathbf r)$ of [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]] is Hermitian with trace one. Conversely, every Hermitian trace-one matrix $\rho\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ has a unique vector $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^3$ such that
$$\rho=\rho(\mathbf r)=\frac12\bigl(I+r_xX+r_yY+r_zZ\bigr).$$
For a qubit density operator this vector is exactly $(\operatorname{tr}(\rho X),\operatorname{tr}(\rho Y),\operatorname{tr}(\rho Z))$, the coordinate map of [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. In particular all three trace coordinates of every density operator are real.
proof_obligations: Use {I,X,Y,Z} as an orthogonal real basis of Hermitian 2x2 matrices.

items.title: Pauli formula for an axis rotation
items.statement_or_definition:
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)\in\mathbb R^3$ with $\|\mathbf n\|_2=1$, put $\Sigma=\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}=n_xX+n_yY+n_zZ$. Then
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\Sigma\right)=\cos(\theta/2)I-i\sin(\theta/2)\Sigma,$$
and $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$ is unitary. For the endpoint $\theta=0$, it equals $I$.
proof_obligations: Use (n·sigma)^2=I in the exponential series and multiply by the adjoint.

items.title: Hadamard conjugation of the Pauli matrices
items.statement_or_definition:
For $H$ as defined in [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]],
$$HXH=Z,\qquad HZH=X,\qquad HYH=-Y.$$
Moreover, if $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $|-\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, then $H|0\rangle=|+\rangle$, $H|1\rangle=|-\rangle$, and $|+\rangle,|-\rangle$ are the $+1$ and $-1$ eigenvectors of $X$, respectively. Thus $H$ sends the computational basis to the $X$-eigenbasis.
proof_obligations: Multiply the stated matrices and verify the minus sign and normalization.

items.title: The Bloch ball is exactly the qubit density-state space
items.statement_or_definition:
For every $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^3$, $\rho(\mathbf r)$ from [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]] is a qubit density operator if and only if $\|\mathbf r\|_2\le1$. Its eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are
$$\lambda_\pm=\frac{1\pm\|\mathbf r\|_2}{2}.$$
The **Bloch ball** is $\{\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^3:\|\mathbf r\|_2\le1\}$; its boundary $\{\|\mathbf r\|_2=1\}$ is the **Bloch sphere**.
proof_obligations: Square r·sigma using anticommutation and compute its eigenvalues, including r=0.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)

items.title: Purity is the boundary of the Bloch ball
items.statement_or_definition:
If $\rho$ is a qubit density operator and $\mathbf r$ is its unique Bloch vector, then
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho^2)=\frac{1+\|\mathbf r\|_2^2}{2}.$$
The state $\rho$ is pure, meaning it is the projector of a pure-state ray, if and only if $\|\mathbf r\|_2=1$.
proof_obligations: For a density, eigenvalues are nonnegative and sum one, so tr(rho²)=1 iff precisely one eigenvalue is one; use rank-one density/ray theorem. Pauli trace multiplication gives the displayed formula.

title: Qubits, Bloch Sphere, Pauli Algebra, and One-Qubit Gates — Examples

items.title: Bloch coordinates of |0> and H|0>
items.statement_or_definition: Let $\rho_0=|0\rangle\langle0|$. Apply $H$ to obtain $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $\rho_+=|+\rangle\langle+|$. The Bloch vectors are $(0,0,1)$ and $(1,0,0)$, respectively, and both states lie on the Bloch sphere.
proof_obligations: Compute the three Pauli expectations and verify the radius and purity identities.
